# Local changes to mermaid-rs-renderer 0.3.1

Upstream: crates.io `mermaid-rs-renderer` 0.3.1 (git `2f993bd79a55235eb59a34d807852276ba25bea7`),
MIT, see `LICENSE`. This copy is a library-only path dependency of `ssw-render`; the directory is
excluded from the workspace and keeps its own lints and tests.

## Changes

| # | Change | Where | Regression test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Removed the `cli` and `png` features and their code (clap, resvg, CLI `main.rs`/`cli.rs`). The CLI's private `merge_init_config` is re-implemented by `ssw-render` (`crates/ssw-render/src/mermaid.rs`, `apply_config`). | `Cargo.toml`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/render.rs` | none (removal) |
| 2 | Test inputs `docs/comparison_sources/*.mmd` fetched from upstream at the pinned commit (the crates.io package omits them) so upstream's own unit tests compile. | `docs/comparison_sources/` | upstream suite |
| 3 | The on-disk font cache is opt-in. Upstream copied system font files to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/mmdr/font-cache` or `$HOME/.cache/mmdr/font-cache` on first use (an editor must not write there unasked, and a stale cache makes layout depend on history). Now it is only used when `MMDR_FONT_CACHE_DIR` is set. | `src/text_metrics.rs` `cache_paths` | none: the cache path is environment configuration, no behavior change in measurement |
| 4 | **Gantt scheduling and axis.** Root cause of the 44-year axis / zero-width bars: `compute_gantt_layout` kept a running `cursor` of *absolute* day numbers and placed every task without a start at `origin + cursor`, adding the chart origin twice (the `:24d` task of the docs example started in 2057 and stretched the axis). Scheduling is now `schedule_gantt` (start = own date, else latest end of the `after` tasks, else end of the previous task, else earliest chart date; end = end date, `until` task start, or calendar-aware start + duration; forward references, multiple `after` ids, reference cycles). `dateFormat` (moment subset incl. `HH:mm`, `MMM`, `X`/`x`, `[..]`) is parsed per chart and a token is a date only if it parses under it (ids such as `task-1`, `v1.2` are no longer dates); ids keep their case; durations follow Mermaid units (`m` minutes, `M` months, `ms s h d w y`); `axisFormat` (d3 `%Y %m %d %b %B %a %e %H %M %-d ...`) and `tickInterval` are honoured, otherwise the finest calendar spacing whose labels do not collide is chosen (weeks start Sunday). Unsupported: `excludes`/`includes`, `todayMarker`, `crit`+`active` combination (last tag wins). | `src/gantt_time.rs` (new), `src/parser.rs` `parse_gantt_diagram`/`parse_gantt_task_meta`/`gantt_directive`, `src/ir.rs` (`GanttTask.end/until`, `Graph.gantt_date_format/axis_format/tick_interval`), `src/layout/gantt.rs` `schedule_gantt`/`gantt_date_ticks`/`compute_gantt_layout` | `gantt_time::tests::*`; `layout::gantt::tests::docs_example_schedules_every_task_on_its_own_dates`, `docs_example_axis_spans_fifty_days_and_bars_have_their_width`, `docs_example_axis_labels_use_axis_format_and_stay_on_the_chart`, `axis_format_and_tick_interval_directives_are_honoured`, `task_without_start_follows_the_previous_task`, `references_use_exact_ids_forward_references_and_the_latest_end`, `calendar_months_and_clock_times_are_scheduled_exactly`, `charts_without_dates_count_days_from_zero`, ...; `parser::tests::parse_gantt_task_tokens_follow_the_date_format`; `ssw-render` `tests/mermaid_fixtures.rs::gantt_fixture_axis_covers_its_three_weeks` |
| 5 | **Sequence `-)`, `--)`, `-x`, `--x` messages were dropped** (not in the arrow list; `A-)J` produced no edge). `parse_sequence_message` now looks for the leftmost arrow in the part before the first `:` (message text such as `a->b` is no longer taken for the arrow); `-)`/`--)` are drawn like `->>`/`-->>`, `-x`/`--x` end in a cross decoration. | `src/parser.rs` `parse_sequence_message`, `SEQUENCE_MESSAGE_ARROWS` | `parser::tests::parse_sequence_async_and_lost_arrows`, `parse_sequence_reversed_arrows_swap_the_endpoints`; `layout::sequence::tests::async_and_lost_messages_are_drawn_between_their_lifelines` |
| 6 | **Sequence frame swallowed the note written before it** (the spike's "loop frame drawn before the first message, label on autonumber circle 1"). A note and a following `loop` share the message index; layout took every note with `start_idx <= index <= end_idx` into the frame, so with `Note right of J` before `loop` the frame started at `note.y - 82.8 px`, above "Hello John" (SVG evidence: loop rect `y=103.70`, first message `y=130.5`, circle 1 at `y=118.6` inside the label tab `103.7..123.7`). Notes now carry the ids of the frames open when they were written (`SequenceNote.frames`, `SequenceFrame.id`); layout uses them. A note after `end` also starts below the frame's bottom padding instead of on its border. | `src/ir.rs`, `src/parser.rs` `parse_sequence_diagram`, `src/layout/sequence.rs` `compute_sequence_layout` | `parser::tests::parse_sequence_notes_remember_the_frames_they_are_in`; `layout::sequence::tests::docs_example_frames_enclose_only_their_own_messages`, `note_written_before_a_loop_stays_outside_the_loop_frame`, `note_inside_a_frame_extends_it`, `note_after_end_is_not_part_of_the_frame`, `autonumber_circles_stay_clear_of_frame_labels` |
| 7 | **Sequence shorthand `B-->>-A` deactivated the receiver** (A) and left B's bar open to the end of the diagram. Mermaid's `-` ends the *sender's* activation. | `src/parser.rs` `parse_sequence_diagram` | `parser::tests::parse_sequence_shorthand_deactivation_ends_the_senders_bar`; `layout::sequence::tests::shorthand_deactivation_closes_the_bar_the_plus_opened` |
| 8 | **Flowchart `cycle_fixture_subgraph_entry_aligns_with_spine`: assertion relaxed to one port step (no router change).** Trace (diagnostic run, Windows/Segoe UI): `H->F` is an outer back edge on F's *left* side (`(315.2,619.8)..(62.2,667.8)(62.2,619.8)`), so F's top side carries only `E->F`; the initial port assignment therefore gives offset 0 (the earlier "two edges on F's top" analysis was wrong, and a port-ordering tie-break written on that premise changed nothing and was reverted). The +16 px comes from the refinement stage (`refine_flowchart_ports_with_route_candidates`, which also tries `ideal +- step`): the straight line at x = 105.4 runs through the subgraph title obstacle built by `build_label_obstacles_for_routing` (`x = sub.x + 12 - 3 .. + label_w + 6` with `sub.x = 32.2`, `label_w = 84.0` for "LoopBlock" with Segoe UI, i.e. 41.2..131.2, y 530.8..560.8; E->F crosses y 530.8..560.8 between E and F), so it shifts the port by one 16 px step. The width of that obstacle is font-metric dependent, which is why upstream (other font) gets a straight line. The test now requires at most one jog of one port step; the new `cycle_fixture_entry_is_straight_when_the_subgraph_title_is_not_in_the_way` renames the subgraph to `L` and asserts the straight 2-point line, which is the check of this explanation. | `src/layout/mod.rs` tests only | `cycle_fixture_subgraph_entry_aligns_with_spine` (relaxed), `cycle_fixture_entry_is_straight_when_the_subgraph_title_is_not_in_the_way` (new) |

## Reproduction results (Windows 11, Segoe UI metrics, default options)

* **Sequence duplicate participant columns: does not reproduce.** `participant A as Alice` / `actor J as John` parse to the ids `A`,`J` with labels Alice/John (`parse_sequence_participant`); `.tmp/diag-seq.svg` has each name exactly twice (top and bottom boxes), `layout.nodes.len() == 2` (asserted in `docs_example_frames_enclose_only_their_own_messages`). Not fixed because nothing is broken; the spike most likely read the footbox row as duplicates. `actor` is still drawn as a box (upstream maps it to `ActorBox`): cosmetic, not changed.
* **Gantt**: reproduced and fixed (row 4). **Sequence ordering / label collision**: reproduced and fixed (row 6). **`-)` dropped**: reproduced and fixed (row 5).
* Known remaining sequence limitation: a note written as the *first* line inside a frame is placed before the frame's top gap, so the frame's top edge can run over the message above it (frame geometry is relative to the first message, not the note).

## Unverified
Rows 4-7 were desk-checked and passed in the orchestrator's 06:25 run (360 passed). Row 8: the numbers above come from a diagnostic test run; that the title obstacle is the cause is inferred from them and is checked by the new `cycle_fixture_entry_is_straight_when_the_subgraph_title_is_not_in_the_way` (if it fails, the cause is something else and the relaxed assertion is not justified). Not changed: `actor` is drawn as a box, not a stick figure.
